orchestrator or the runs themselves (the user's standing rule, STATUS §6) and are recorded in each run's report.

Run 1 – the Ugaritic myths (report: run-1.md)

Settled by the orchestrator (minor, under the user's standing rule): the run's 21 philological cruxes (its
"Questions for the user" table: nʿl il, ḫnzr, psltm, mtm, bṯ, bʿlm, yw, l ydʿt, mt "husband", the
damaged ṣlmm, …) are matters of reading, each translated with the defensible choice first and the alternative in its
note (guidelines §6.8, a crux). They stay as drafted; the user may revisit any of them when reviewing the draft. The
yw note (most scholars reject a link with YHWH) stays as written.

No question from run 1 needs the user.

Run 3 – Egyptian wisdom and creation (report: run-3.md)

Settled by the orchestrator (minor, under the user's standing rule): the run's five optional points are kept as
drafted – Amenemope's twr split by construction (הִנָּזֵר מִן / הוֹקִיר / נִטְהַר: no one Hebrew verb holds all
three senses); "true of voice" in AM 2.8, 2.12 left open in the notes; the Memphite Theology's ḥtp = נח in every verbal
use (so Ptah's "rest" in line 59 stays visible as the same word – the comparison with Gen 2:2 needs it); the Heavenly
Cow 15, 27 on the TLA's reading, marked ?, with Hornung's in the note; Merikare E134 on the base text (pCarlsberg),
with pMoscow's "in the egg" in the note.

No question from run 3 needs the user.

Run 4 – Hesiod (report: run-4.md)

For the user (optional; nothing waits on it – the current choice is in place and reversible by one table edit and a
script pass):

  1. Hesiod's speaking names – the cosmic names and abstractions are translated as names, without the article
    (Χάος פַּעַר, Γαῖα אֶרֶץ, Οὐρανός שָׁמַיִם, Νύξ לַיְלָה, Ἔρις מָדוֹן, Δίκη מִשְׁפָּט …), as West and Most do in
    English, so the reader hears what a Greek hearer heard. The alternative is to transcribe every name (כָאוֹס, גַּאיָה,
    אוּרָנוֹס …), as the existing Hebrew translations do. Which should the Hebrew reader meet? (הסיודוס/renderings.md
    §3.2, §12.1)

Settled by the orchestrator (minor): the command infinitive as the infinitive absolute (עֲבוֹד, קָצוֹר) stays – it
is the closest Hebrew to the Greek form and it reads as elevated, not as an error; αἰδώς בּוּשָׁה, τιμαί זְכֻיּוֹת,
εὐδαίμων בַּר־מַזָּל stay, each with its note; the folder's spelling stays as it is (אשה; qamaṣ qaṭan per the existing
corpora); lines the base does not bracket stay without {חשודה}, with the modern athetesis in the note.
